agent.name: Organizational Adoption Agent
agent.specialty: Organizational readiness for emerging technology adoption

analytical_question: Can this organization govern and sustain the proposed packaging RFQ drafting assistant, and what must change before the next adoption decision?
general_et_finding: LLM-generated text can include plausible factual errors or fabricated references. NIST identifies this risk as confabulation. No evidence in the intake establishes the selected model's accuracy.
application_finding: An evidence-linked draft could reduce bid comparison effort if buyers can trace and verify prices, terms, and omissions. A read-only historical test with manual approval and fallback bounds the exposure. Fit remains conditional on use-specific evaluation.
organization_specific_finding:
Leadership and sponsorship: Partial. Director endorsement exists, with no delegation.
Skills and training: Partial. Buyers know sourcing policy and lack AI verification rehearsal.
Workflow and process: Partial. Manual sign-off exists, with no AI review or exception handoff.
Infrastructure and data: Partial. Security approved sanitized inputs and a sandbox is available. Some IDs and revisions failed the spot check.
Resources and budget: Gap. No review time or pilot budget is allocated.
Governance and risk: Gap. There is no escalation step or authorized stop decision-maker.
Culture and change: Unknown. Buyer questions show that expectations for error reporting are unresolved.
Operating ownership: Gap. The organization has designated no pilot owner.

evidence.claim: Confabulation is a documented generative AI risk. NIST also offers guidance on acceptable use and feedback mechanisms.
evidence.source_or_reference: NIST AI 600-1, section 2.2 and actions GV-3.2-003 and GV-3.2-004, https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1
evidence.notes: General risk and oversight guidance. The adoption decisions are specialist judgments from the fictional profiles.

evidence.claim: The director supports the idea. No owner, stop authority, pilot funding, or protected time is in place.
evidence.notes: Explicit gaps that block a controlled trial.

evidence.claim: Buyers know manual sourcing policy and the team has a sandbox with approved sanitized data. Some source IDs and revision labels are missing.
evidence.notes: Existing resources reduce setup work. Approval of the inputs for use does not establish traceability.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: The approved sandbox and manual sign-off are useful starting conditions. No packet error rate, reviewer workload, or culture assessment was supplied.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in HOLD within the scenario because several controls are explicitly absent. Low confidence in the time and cost needed to close them.
value_opportunity_implication: Measure buyer minutes for drafting plus verification and correction against a manual baseline. Count material omissions and corrections alongside time saved.
risk_governance_implication: If an incorrect brief or access incident occurs, the current profile lacks an accountable stop and escalation path. Keep procurement work in the existing manual process.
recommendation_management_implication: HOLD the four-week pilot. 1. Procurement director should sign a charter naming an accountable operator, stop decision-maker, and escalation backup. Verify the route in a tabletop exercise. 2. Sponsor should fund the sandbox and protect reviewer hours. Category manager should rehearse source checks, manual fallback, and safe error reporting with buyers before sign-off. 3. Proposed procurement data steward should reconcile supplier IDs and bid revisions to approved sources and exclude unresolved packets. Reassess pilot readiness after all three close.
change_monitoring_triggers: At the next readiness review, inspect signed stop authority and the escalation rehearsal record. Keep HOLD if either is missing.
Reassess once reviewer capacity is funded, the review and fallback rehearsal passes, and each admitted packet has verified supplier IDs and revision labels.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Who will have authority to pause the pilot and cover incidents, and can the procurement director provide the signed delegation and escalation procedure? The current absence blocks pilot launch.
What protected buyer hours and budget will the sponsor commit? Provide an allocation and staffing plan before reconsidering pilot approval.
